subject: Clarifying DPA incident notification: subprocessors & cross-border handoffs
messages:
From: Rajiv Nair <rajiv.nair@globebank.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, security@redwood.com
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@globebank.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Potential data exposure affecting EU customers - initial flags

Hi Ava / Redwood security team,

We have received an alert from our internal monitoring indicating unusual access patterns against the sandbox workload that processes EU customer PII. At this stage we do not have confirmed exfiltration, but logs show repeated API calls from an IP range that doesn't match our partners. Can you confirm whether Redwood saw any automated job restarts or configuration changes in the EU cluster between 2026-02-09 22:00 UTC and 2026-02-10 02:00 UTC?

Given contractual DPA language (Section 7.2 in our agreement), GlobeBank requires notification of any incident that "reasonably results in unauthorized access to personal data" and cooperation with forensic evidence transfer. Please advise the expected timeline for a substantive update and what evidence you can provide if this escalates.

We appreciate a quick acknowledgement and an initial scope indication.

Thanks,
Rajiv Nair
Head of Cloud Security, GlobeBank
security@globebank.com

Attachment: none

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Rajiv Nair <rajiv.nair@globebank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure affecting EU customers - initial flags

Rajiv — thanks for flagging and for the clear citation to the DPA clause. Acknowledged.

Quick answers: we have no automated job restarts recorded in the EU production pool during the window you cite, and no immediate signs of mass data export in our tokenized logs. That said, we will kick off a scoped forensic check focused on: 1) API access patterns for the mentioned workload, 2) KV cache access events, and 3) any abnormal model IO beyond expected token count.

Operational plan:
- Internal triage started (SEC-412).
- Forensic snapshot request queued with infra; tentative ETA for first forensic artifacts: 24-36 hours.
- We will provide an initial "we are investigating" notice to GlobeBank within 12 hours and a substantive update within 72 hours or sooner if we confirm unauthorized access.

To align on contractual language and expectations, cc'ing Kimberly (Legal/Privacy) and Marissa (Customer Ops). Do you have a preferred evidence transfer method (S3 presigned, encrypted courier, or via your legal upload)? Also: are there specific data types or subsystems you are most concerned about (PII, payment tokens, audit logs)?

Ava Chen
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

Attachments: forensic-request-template.pdf (template we'll use for evidence handoff)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure - DPA obligations and redline suggestion

Team — drafting quick recommended language to align ops with the GlobeBank DPA and to reduce ambiguity around subprocessors and cross-border handoffs. Proposal below (for internal review before we send anything formal to the customer):

Proposed incident notification & cooperation text (draft):
"Upon becoming aware of an event that reasonably may constitute unauthorized access to personal data covered by this DPA, Redwood will: (a) provide an acknowledgement to the Customer within twenty‑four (24) hours of such awareness summarizing the initial scope and steps being taken; (b) provide a substantive update within seventy‑two (72) hours of determination of incident scope, including affected data types and an initial assessment of impact; (c) cooperate with reasonable Customer requests for forensic evidence and provide access to relevant logs and snapshots from Redwood or any implicated subprocessor within forty‑eight (48) hours of a formal request; and (d) where evidence transfer requires cross‑border transfer, Redwood will either: (i) transfer via an agreed secure channel and provide export documentation, or (ii) facilitate temporary on‑site forensic access at a mutually agreed location, subject to applicable law."

Operational notes:
- The 24h/72h split preserves the ability to send a short, non-actionable acknowledgement quickly while buying time for a substantive determination.
- The 48h evidence window assumes subprocessor cooperation; if a subprocessor contract prevents timely evidence transfer we need escalation language and a defined exception path.
- For EU customers, cross‑border transfer must honor SCCs; include preservation of audit trail and redaction rules for non-GlobeBank data.

Open questions for Ops: can we commit to the 48h evidence turnaround for subprocessors in all EU regions, or do we need a region-by-region exception map? Ben — please confirm realistic timelines for evidence collection and export when subprocessors are involved.

Kimberly
VP, Legal & Privacy, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: timeline-draft.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 13:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure - DPA obligations and redline suggestion

Kimberly / Ava — quick operational confirmation after checking infra and subprocessor SLAs:

- Internal evidence collection (snapshots, request logs) — 24-36 hours typical for EU clusters.
- Direct evidence from first-party services — we can provide within 48 hours.
- Subprocessor evidence: depends on contract; 48 hours is attainable only if the subprocessor has a predefined forensic intake (many do not). For subprocessors without an intake SLA we should set an expectation of "best effort with escalation to account/partner ops" and document exceptions.
- Cross-border mechanics: for transfers out of the EU, we require either the customer's SCCs or an approved export path; if GlobeBank prefers on-site review, add a clause about travel & cost allocation.

Recommended next steps:
1) Send GlobeBank an interim acknowledgement (Ava to send within 12 hours as promised).
2) Share the redline clause above with GlobeBank Legal as a proposed DPA amendment (Kimberly).
3) Start a quick audit of our top EU subprocessors to identify which have forensic intake SLAs; publish a short exception table. (Marissa to own, target 5 business days.)

If GlobeBank signs off on the 24/72/48 structure we should include a short exception appendix listing subprocessors that may require extra time.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability & Forensics, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Forwarding plan: once we have Kimberly's approval on wording, Ava please send a customer-facing note that contains: (1) acknowledgement, (2) what we can commit to in this incident, and (3) the proposed DPA redline for review.
